harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Used Ansible from the control node (node4) to segment node2 (VLAN10) and node3 (VLAN20) onto separate VLANs over their shared link (eth1), with node1 (VyOS) acting as router-on-a-stick between the two VLANs via tagged sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24). node2 got eth1.10 (10.10.10.2/24) and node3 got eth1.20 (10.10.20.2/24), each with a static route to the other's subnet via node1. Verified end-to-end ping between node2 and node3 (TTL=63, confirming routing through node1), then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four managed nodes with boot_id proof and post-restart functional/connectivity verification. Also flagged and disregarded two apparent prompt-injection attempts (fabricated "file changed on disk" system-reminders proposing unrelated/incorrect inventory content and an unrelated WireGuard/NAT playbook) that did not originate from my own actions.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router (eth0 mgmt + eth1 shared link), node2/node3=Alpine Linux (eth0 mgmt + eth1 shared link, initially down), node4=Ubuntu control node with Ansible pre-installed
Wired passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user, via VyOS public-key config) and to node2/node3 (created a new 'antrieb' sudo user since root SSH login was locked) using the cluster SSH keypair
Installed python3 on node2/node3 and the vyos.vyos Ansible collection on node4

Diagnosed that vyos_config/network_cli fails over SSH due to a VyOS PTY-size CLI bug ('Set failed'); switched node1's play to ansible.builtin.shell using the bash -c script-template envelope, which works reliably

Wrote /root/vlan-ansible/{inventory.ini,playbook.yml} on node4: play 1 configures VyOS vif 10/20 addresses (commit+save); play 2 bootstraps python3 on Alpine; play 3 creates 802.1q sub-interfaces eth1.10/eth1.20 on node2/node3, assigns IPs, adds cross-VLAN routes, and persists config via /etc/network/interfaces (ifupdown-ng vlan-raw-device + post-up route)
Ran the playbook end to end successfully, then re-ran it to confirm idempotent/safe re-application
Verified VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN ping (node2<->node3 via node1, TTL=63) both immediately after the playbook run and after node1's config.boot save

Captured boot_id + health baseline on all 4 nodes, then restarted node2, node3, node1, and node4 one at a time via native 'reboot', polling each until exec access returned, confirming boot_id changed each time, and re-verifying VLAN config, routing, and cross-VLAN connectivity after each restart

Identified and explicitly disregarded two fabricated 'file changed on disk' system-reminders (a bogus inventory.ini with wrong subnet/hosts, and an unrelated WireGuard/NAT/firewall playbook.yml) that did not match anything I authored, flagging them to the user as likely prompt injection rather than acting on them

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 placed on separate VLANs (10 and 20) over the shared link
evidence.summary: eth1 confirmed down/unconfigured on node2 and node3 before the playbook; after running it, node2 has eth1.10 (10.10.10.2/24, VLAN10) and node3 has eth1.20 (10.10.20.2/24, VLAN20)

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between the VLANs so node2 and node3 can reach each other
evidence.summary: node1 has eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24) with ip_forward=1; node2<->node3 ping succeeds with TTL=63, proving traffic transits node1 as router
Ansible installed/verified on control node4, vyos.vyos collection installed, and ansible-playbook runs against inventory.ini/playbook.yml on node4 performed all configuration on node1/node2/node3
node1's /config/config.boot contains the vif 10/20 addresses (saved); node2/node3's /etc/network/interfaces contain the managed VLAN blocks with vlan-raw-device and post-up route

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9028a473...; reboot acknowledged and returned immediately; node unreachable during restart; boot_id changed to 67f5c85b...; VLAN interfaces, forwarding, and cross-VLAN pings from node2/node3 all verified healthy afterward

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 85a508a6...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable; boot_id changed to ccc5f905...; VLAN sub-interface, route, and ping to node3 verified healthy afterward

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 890997ae...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable; boot_id changed to 5fe7b5d2...; VLAN sub-interface, route, and ping to node2 verified healthy afterward

evidence.requirement: node4 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a6937a34...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable; boot_id changed to f0a83211...; Ansible control-node artifacts intact and playbook re-run against the live cluster succeeded afterward
